cases.title: A roll of 3 releases nothing; the turn passes (BR-04, BR-13)
A roll of 6 releases a token to its start cell and grants an extra roll (BR-04, BR-06)
With releaseOnOne, a roll of 1 also releases a token, but grants no extra turn (BR-04 variant)
With extraTurnOnSix off, a release on 6 ends the turn (BR-06 disablable)
Capturing an opponent token grants an extra roll (BR-06, BR-08)
With extraTurnOnCapture off, a capture ends the turn (BR-06 disablable)
Moving a token home grants an extra roll (BR-06, BR-10)
With extraTurnOnHome off, reaching home ends the turn (BR-06 disablable)
The third consecutive six is shown but not played; the turn passes (BR-07)
With maxConsecutiveSixes 0, the third six is an ordinary roll (BR-07 variant)
Landing on a non-safe cell occupied by an opponent captures it (BR-08)
Landing on a start cell (track 13, safe) captures nothing; both colours share the cell (BR-09)
Landing on a star cell (track 8, safe) captures nothing (BR-09)
Landing on a non-safe cell captures every opponent token there (BR-08)
Passing over an opponent token never captures it (BR-05, BR-08)
With exact finish, a roll overshooting home makes that token illegal (BR-10)
With exactFinish off, an overshooting roll still lands the token home (BR-10 variant)
A six with no legal move still grants its extra roll; the same player rolls again (BR-13)
Crossing step 51 enters the own home path (step 53 is home-path index 1) (BR-10, D-20)
Bringing the fourth token home wins and the match ends (BR-11)
Applying a move that is not legal throws and leaves the state unchanged (FR-21, BR-10)
Two tokens of the same colour may share a cell; no blockade (BR-12)
Six, move, six, move, six: the third six in the sequence is not played and the turn passes (BR-07)
